chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“If the thief comes of his own accord, repenting to Allah, and returns what he stole to its owner, then there is no amputation upon him.”

key_terms.إِلَى اللَّهِ: to Allah; indicating sincere tawbah directed to Him
key_terms.اَلسَّارِقُ: the thief; the person who committed theft
key_terms.تَائِبًا: repenting; returning to Allah in remorse
key_terms.سَرِقَتَهُ: what he stole; the stolen property
key_terms.صَاحِبِهَا: its owner; the rightful possessor of the property
key_terms.قَطْعَ: amputation; the prescribed hadd punishment for theft

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment dropped if a thief repents and returns the stolen property before being taken up?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a thief voluntarily comes forward in repentance to Allah and restores the stolen property to its owner, the prescribed amputation is not carried out against him. It highlights the legal and moral significance of sincere tawbah and restitution of others’ rights.
